bandReport.notes: Q109 opens cleanly at the top of p20's left column with its number and full stem — nothing continues in from p19. Q120 ends with its option (d) followed only by the footer, and the paper genuinely ends at Q120: the source PDF has 22 pages (0-based indices 0-21), so my p21 (index 21) is the LAST page in the file, and there is no content of any kind below Q120(d). Two caveats about that final page, both harmless: it still prints '[ P.T.O.' in the footer, which is boilerplate on every page of this booklet rather than a pointer to a missing page; and the printed page numbers jump 41 (p20) -> 43 (p21), i.e. printed page 42 is the blank verso and is not scanned. Nothing in my band belongs to a neighbouring band. TWO-COLUMN HAZARD, verified rather than eyeballed: at the foot of p20 the options of Q112 (left column) and Q115 (right column) INTERLEAVE line-for-line, and the PDF text layer merges them into single blocks reading '(a) sexual harassment in the work- (a) 1 only'. I re-separated them by word-level x-coordinate (left column x<300, right column x>300) and confirmed Q112 = sexual harassment/Sati/dowry death/rape and Q115 = 1 only/2 and 3 only/1 and 2 only/1, 2 and 3. The same check was run on p21, where it matters more: Q118 (left) and Q119 (right) BOTH have an option whose text is '1 only', so a column swap there would have been invisible — confirmed Q118 = 1 only/2 and 3/3 only/1 and 4 and Q119 = 1 only/2 only/Both 1 and 2/Neither 1 nor 2, with Q120's options (improve/diminish/remain constant/first diminish and then improve) sitting in the right column below Q118's block.

flags: catalog-gap: HINDU rock-cut cave architecture (Elephanta, Ellora's Shaiva caves, Badami) has no dedicated subtopic — the only religious-architecture subtopic is scoped to 'Buddhism, Jainism and Religious Architecture', which is the closest fit but names neither Hindu nor Shaiva. questions.stem:
Consider the following statements about impact of tax :
1. A tax is shifted forward to consumers if the demand is inelastic relative to supply.
2. A tax is shifted backward to producers if the supply is relatively more inelastic than demand.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.subject: Economics
flags: catalog-gap: this is PUBLIC FINANCE / tax-incidence theory (forward and backward shifting of a tax under elasticity), and the Economics subject has exactly one chapter, 'Indian Economy', whose three subtopics are Five Year Plans, Government Schemes — Agriculture and Livestock, and International Trade and Finance. None covers taxation, public finance or price theory. Filed under the least-bad subtopic; a 'Public Finance, Taxation and Budget' subtopic (or chapter) is needed.
